subject: Stratus AI renewal: reserved surge & throughput commitments
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prep: Stratus renewal — traffic surge forecast and ask

Team —

Quick sync request before I jump on a call with Lina today at 11am PT. Stratus is planning a product launch (new recommendation feature) and has signaled a 3–6x QPS spike during the first 90 days after go‑live. They asked for a proposal that includes:

- Reserved pool uplift (baseline GPUs + committed burst)
- 99th/95th P50 latency guarantees and throughput SLAs for peak windows
- A short-term canary/rollout plan and fallback model for reliability

I attached the preliminary QPS/tokens forecast they shared (stratus-qps-forecast.csv). From our side I want: a recommended GPU count (baseline + burst), impact on monthly committed spend, and a suggested term (12 vs 24 months + runway credits).

Key facts from intake call:
- Current steady QPS: ~180 requests/sec (avg)
- Median tokens per request: 320 tokens; 95th percentile tokens: ~1,250 tokens
- Planned launch: June 15, expected initial peak multiplier: 3x, with potential to reach 6x within 60 days if adoption strong

Can Rishi run the throughput->GPU calc quick and Karthik draft an ops-friendly rollback policy? Marissa, I'll align on pricing/term options to propose.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Lina Gomez <lina@stratus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prep: Stratus renewal — traffic surge forecast and ask

Soojin —

Thanks for moving quickly. A few clarifications from our side to help calc:

- We expect a hard launch on 2027-06-15 and a marketing-driven traffic spike for the first 30 days. Traffic profile: 11am–2pm PST and 5pm–8pm PST windows for US users, multipliers ~3x during those windows.
- If retention metrics look good, traffic could continue rising to 5–6x by month two (organic growth / retention).
- We plan to increase prompt complexity for personalized recs in July (that pushes avg tokens/request to ~420).

We want a proposal that:
1) Guarantees baseline throughput for 95% of the day (our core app traffic) with a committed reserved pool.
2) Includes a short burst pool (on-demand reserved credits) to cover sustained peaks up to 6x for up to 72 hours total in a month.
3) Has an optional 30% discount tier if we move to a 24‑month commit.

I attached the CSV you requested. Can you send a recommended configuration + cost ballpark by EOD tomorrow?

—Lina
Procurement Lead, Stratus AI
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prep: Stratus renewal — traffic surge forecast and ask

Team — I ran a throughput model off the CSV and our kernel benchmarks. Summary (rounded):

Assumptions
- Target model family: 13B fine-tuned instruction model (baseline perf profile).
- Effective tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv under our runtime (with batching/kv cache): ~18k tokens/sec sustained at 90% util for latency <350ms p95.
- Typical request tokens: 320 -> initial; 420 tokens starting month 2 as Lina noted.

Forecasted load (peak windows):
- Current baseline peak: 180 qps * 320 tokens = 57,600 tokens/sec peak
- Launch (3x peak during windows): 540 qps * 320 = 172,800 tokens/sec
- Month 2 (up to 6x; higher tokens): 1,080 qps * 420 = 453,600 tokens/sec

Capacity recommendation
- Baseline reserved pool: 6 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs -> sustained capacity ~108,000 tokens/sec (covers steady/day 95% traffic with headroom).
- Committed burst pool: additional 8 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs available on short notice (reserved credits) -> combined reserved = 14 GPUs -> combined sustained capacity ~252,000 tokens/sec. This covers launch 3x peaks comfortably and provides partial coverage for month-2 growth.
- Temporary surge plan (short lived spikes up to 6x): use our burst-on-demand offering to add up to 10 extra GPUs for up to 72 hours/month. With full burst (24 GPUs total) we hit ~432,000 tokens/sec which gets within 95% of the projected month-2 worst-case.

SLO notes
- With 14 GPUs reserved we can guarantee a 95th latency SLO of <350ms for windows up to 3x traffic. For sustained 6x events latency will degrade unless burst GPUs added; recommend automated fallback to a smaller model variant for degraded windows (see rollback below).

Rollback / canary ops (Karthik please expand):
- Stage traffic to prod in three waves (10% / 40% / 100%) over 72 hours.
- Automated health checks: p95 latency, error rate, and token cost per request.
- If p95 exceeds 500ms or error rate >1.5% for 10min, automatically route a share of traffic to 'reduced' model variant (6B quantized profile) and notify on-call.

Cost/term sketch
- 12-month commit: base reserved 6 GPUs + committed burst credits for 8 GPUs = baseline monthly commit $XXXk (see attachment redwood-gpu-recommendation.pdf).
- 24-month commit: propose 20–30% discount on reserved base + increased burst credits at no additional margin to help runway.

I'll inline a short recommendation doc and cost bands; Marissa can firm up pricing/discount structure.

—Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@stratus.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed renewal & surge package (term sheet attached)

Lina / Team —

Thanks for the details and Rishi’s fast turnaround. Attached is the proposal with three options (short summary below and full pricing in attached PDF):

Option A — 12‑month (conservative)
- Reserved: 6 A100-equiv GPUs
- Committed burst credits: 8 GPUs (avail on 15min ramp)
- On-demand surge: up to +10 GPUs for 72 hours/month at preferential rate
- 95th latency SLO <350ms for up to 3x sustained windows
- Monthly commit: $198,000 (est)

Option B — 24‑month (recommended for runway)
- Reserved: 8 A100-equiv GPUs
- Committed burst credits: 10 GPUs
- On-demand surge: up to +12 GPUs for 96 hours/month included
- 95th latency SLO <320ms for up to 3x sustained windows; extended support SLA
- 24‑month price reduction: 25% off base reserved list; monthly commit: $148,500 (est)

Option C — Aggressive growth (for enterprise scale)
- Reserved: 14 GPUs (all reserved)
- No reliance on on-demand surge; includes priority capacity routing and guaranteed throughput for 6x events up to 48 hours
- Monthly commit: $360,000 (est)

Next steps
1) Review options with your engineering and finance teams; tell us which option you prefer as a baseline.
2) If you want the rollout plan tied to the purchase order, we can lock in a staged deployment (10% -> 40% -> 100%) and include a 30‑day transition credit to cover extra burst during ramp.
3) If procurement agrees to a 24‑month term, we'll prepare a formal contract (term-sheet v3 attached) and queue capacity for June 1 to ensure ramp readiness.

Happy to jump on a call to talk through the tradeoffs tomorrow.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: renewal-term-sheet-v3.pdf, redwood-gpu-recommendation.pdf
